prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The five frames show a stable, enclosed operator area: the camera wearer’s forearms, hands, knees and thighs are nearest, roughly 0.3–0.8 m away, with the two controls about 0.4–0.6 m ahead and left/right of the body; the front crossbar, protective side grids and machine structure lie roughly 0.7–1.5 m away, while the ground beyond is farther, approximately 2 m or more. A second person is only partly visible near the upper-right edge outside the enclosure, likely about 1–2 m from the camera wearer, but the crop prevents reliable facing or gaze estimation. Across the strip there is little large-scale approach or retreat: the cabin remains fixed relative to the wearer, while modest viewpoint changes shift the controls, limbs and exterior structure laterally. The depth map makes near-versus-far layering and the occlusion of the exterior by the wearer, controls, bars and grids clearer than RGB, but its absolute metre estimates are uncertain and it appears unreliable on thin bars, grid openings, image borders and some bright exterior surfaces.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map separates several foreground person regions corresponding mainly to the camera wearer’s arms and lower body, positioned centrally and on both sides within arm’s reach, while broad blue-gray regions trace parts of the surrounding machine and protective enclosure about 0.5–1.5 m away. It also intermittently labels controls or machinery as “motorcycle,” and in the middle frame marks small nearby regions as “cell phone” and “cup”; comparison with RGB suggests these object classes are unreliable even though their masks roughly indicate foreground structure near the hands. The wearer and enclosure strongly occlude the ground and anything directly ahead, and the other person in yellow is largely cropped or missed, so their distance, orientation and gaze cannot be recovered reliably from this map. Over the five frames the principal masks shift slightly with the viewpoint but show no clear person-to-person approach or retreat; segmentation clarifies object boundaries and overlap that blend together in RGB, while failing on fragmented limbs, thin cage bars and mislabeled machine parts.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects only magenta hand skeletons, with one cluster near each control in every frame, placing the wearer’s left and right hands roughly shoulder-width apart, about 0.4–0.6 m in front of the camera and within immediate arm’s reach. Their repeated positions show small hand and wrist shifts across time but no major reaching, withdrawal or crossing, and the right hand remains to the right of the left with both below the forward machine structure. No yellow body skeleton is visible and no usable skeleton is detected for the partly cropped person outside, so body orientation, facing direction, gaze, inter-person distance and what lies within the other person’s reach cannot be inferred from this map. Pose makes the hand locations and joint configuration much clearer than RGB, but it is unreliable for the rest of the bodies because of the egocentric crop, self-occlusion, machinery occlusion and missing detections.
